intro: 10 charts from made-up news sites and ads. Each one uses a trick that makes the numbers say something they never said. Spot the trick, fix the chart yourself, and see what's really going on.

tricks.axis: The axis doesn't start at zero
tricks.percap: Raw totals, never divided by population
tricks.cumul: A running total that hides slowing growth
tricks.size: The shape grows in height and width at once
tricks.third: Two things move together because of a third

stages.title: Breezy Lemonade
stages.headline: Breezy Lemonade sales QUADRUPLED in one year!
qopts: True, sales really multiplied
A huge exaggeration: sales grew about 6%
False, sales went down
stages.why: The second bar looks four times taller because the axis starts at 100, not zero. Sales actually went from 102 to 108 thousand cans. That's about 6%.

stages.title: Nova Stock
stages.headline: Nova stock is taking off! Buy before you miss out.
qopts: The stock is at an all-time high
The stock is still way below where it started the year
The stock is flat
stages.why: The chart shows only the last four months, the one stretch where the stock went up. Over the whole year, it fell from $80 to $55.

stages.title: Most Dangerous City
stages.headline: Oakdale is the most dangerous city in the state: the most car crashes!
qopts: Oakdale is still the worst
Oakdale has the fewest crashes per person
All three cities are about the same
stages.why: Oakdale has 3 million residents. Pine Hollow has only 250,000. Of course the big city has more crashes. Per 1,000 residents, Oakdale is actually the lowest.

stages.title: The Routely App
stages.headline: Routely keeps growing faster every single month!
stages.fix: Show me new subscribers each month
qopts: Growth is speeding up
Growth is slowing down every month
There are no new subscribers at all
stages.why: A running total always goes up, because it just keeps adding. But new sign-ups fell from 500 in January to 120 in June.

stages.title: Lumen vs. Glow
stages.headline: Lumen's revenue is double Glow's.
stages.fix: Make the area match the number
qopts: True, but the chart makes it look like 4x
False from the start
Too modest, the gap is bigger than 2x
stages.why: The number is right: 40 is double 20. But the chart doubled the circle's diameter, which makes its area four times bigger, and your eye reads area. Not every misleading chart has a lying headline.

stages.title: Ice Cream and Drowning
stages.headline: Whenever ice cream sales go up, drownings go up too. Ice cream is dangerous!
qopts: Ice cream causes drowning
Summer drives both: people eat more ice cream and swim more
Drowning makes people eat ice cream
stages.why: The two lines move together because a third thing drives both: hot weather. Two things rising together doesn't mean one causes the other.

stages.title: The Office Lunch Vote
stages.source: Team Tacos post in the office Slack
stages.headline: Team Tacos CRUSHED Team Pizza in the office lunch vote!
qopts: A true landslide
A narrow win: 52 to 48
A tie
stages.why: The first bar looks three times taller because the axis starts at 46. The real gap is just 4 points.

stages.title: Winter Is Over
stages.headline: Snowfall in Cedar Peak drops every year: winter is over!
qopts: Snowfall drops steadily
Snowfall bounces up and down, and 95 inches has happened before
Snowfall rises steadily
stages.why: Three falling years in a row can happen by chance. Over 12 years, snowfall bounces around 110 inches, and 95 isn't unusual. That doesn't mean the climate isn't changing. It means this chart isn't evidence either way.

stages.title: The School Grant
stages.headline: North County gets more state school funding than any other county.
qopts: North County gets less than the other two
North County is still on top
They're all about the same
stages.why: North County has 400,000 students. Bay County has 60,000. The total is bigger, but each student's share is the smallest.

stages.title: Boss Level: The Stashly App
stages.headline: Stashly hit one million users, and the chart proves the company has never been better.
qopts: Better than ever
Losing its users: active users fell to less than half
Holding steady
stages.why: "One million sign-ups" counts everyone who ever made an account, even people who deleted it. The people who actually open the app fell from 340,000 to 140,000.
